refDefault.note: American Thyroid Association general adult reference. Upper limit varies by lab/assay (~4.0-4.5 mIU/L); TSH rises with age in older adults. TSH is the first-line screen for thyroid dysfunction.

references.document: Clinical Thyroidology for the Public / Patient Thyroid Information
references.quote: Doctors generally consider the normal TSH range to be about 0.4 to 4.0 mU/L for most adults, though ranges vary by laboratory and increase with age.

why: Pituitary thyrotropin; most sensitive first-line marker of thyroid axis status (primary hypo/hyperthyroidism) and for titrating levothyroxine.

loincs.longName: Thyroxine (T4) free [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma

molarMassRef.note: Thyroxine free acid C15H11I4NO4; used to convert ng/dL to molar pmol/L form (multiply ng/dL by 12.87 -> pmol/L).

refDefault.note: Mayo Clinic Laboratories FRT4 immunoassay adult interval. FT4 also reported in molar pmol/L form (approx 12-22 pmol/L) using thyroxine MW.

why: Free (non-protein-bound) thyroxine; confirms and grades thyroid status alongside TSH, and is the key marker in central (pituitary/hypothalamic) hypothyroidism where TSH is unreliable.

loincs.longName: Triiodothyronine (T3) Free [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma

molarMassRef.note: Triiodothyronine free acid C15H12I3NO4; used to convert pg/mL to molar pmol/L form (multiply pg/mL by 1.536 -> pmol/L).

refDefault.note: Mayo Clinic Laboratories T3FR adult interval. FT3 also reported in molar pmol/L form (approx 3.1-6.8 pmol/L) using triiodothyronine MW.

why: Free biologically active thyroid hormone; helps characterize hyperthyroidism (e.g., T3-toxicosis) and low-T3 states; adds detail beyond TSH/FT4.

molarMassRef.note: Cortisol C21H30O5; used for the molar nmol/L form (multiply ug/dL by 27.59 -> nmol/L).

refDefault.note: DIURNAL analyte: this is the MORNING interval (specimen collected 6 a.m.-10 a.m.) per ARUP. Cortisol peaks early morning and troughs late evening; interpret strictly by draw time. p.m. values are substantially lower. Molar form in nmol/L (approx 166-508 nmol/L).

references.quote: Adult a.m. (6 a.m.-8 a.m. peak) reference ~5-25 mcg/dL; when glucocorticoid deficiency is suspected an 8 a.m. plasma cortisol <10 mcg/dL warrants further study.

why: Primary adrenal glucocorticoid under HPA/ACTH control; morning value screens for adrenal insufficiency (low) and Cushing syndrome (high). Must be interpreted against collection time due to diurnal rhythm.

refDefault.note: MORNING interval: reference range established on specimens drawn 7 a.m.-10 a.m. per Mayo; no established reference values for p.m. draws. ACTH is a 39-aa peptide reported in mass units (pg/mL); no clinically used molar conversion.

references.quote: Reference range 7.2-63 pg/mL, based on samples drawn between 7 a.m.-10 a.m.; no established reference values for p.m. draws.

why: Pituitary corticotropin; paired with morning cortisol it localizes HPA-axis disorders (ACTH-dependent vs independent Cushing, primary vs secondary adrenal insufficiency).

loincs.longName: Somatomedin C [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma

refDefault.ageNote: STRONGLY AGE-BANDED: value shown is the adult male 41-45 year band (patient is ~43 y). IGF-1 declines with age, so the correct band must be selected by age; adjacent 46-50 y male band is 81-263 ng/mL.
refDefault.note: Age- and sex-specific reference interval from Warde Medical Laboratory age table. Reflects integrated growth-hormone (GH) secretion.

references.document: Insulin-Like Growth Factor I (IGF-1) - age/sex reference table
references.quote: Males 41-45 years: 84-270 ng/mL; males 46-50 years: 81-263 ng/mL.

why: GH-dependent hepatic peptide; stable integrated index of growth-hormone status used to screen/monitor acromegaly (high) and adult GH deficiency (low). Must be read against the age/sex-matched band.
